parties: KPI Green Energy Limited (via subsidiary Sun Drops Energia Limited) acquiring DEK
headline: KPI Green Energy's subsidiary Sun Drops Energia to acquire DEK
sum: KPI Green Energy intimated the NSE of a proposed acquisition by its subsidiary Sun Drops Energia Limited. The transaction details, consideration amount, and target company specifics remain to be disclosed in subsequent regulatory filings.
implication: Parent-subsidiary acquisition structures require careful segregation of disclosure duties between parent and subsidiary; verify which entity holds primary regulatory obligation and timeline for additional disclosures under SEBI Listing Rules.
detail: KPI Green Energy Limited, a renewable energy company listed on the NSE, announced via stock exchange intimation that its subsidiary Sun Drops Energia Limited is undertaking a proposed acquisition of DEK. The filing is dated 21 August 2026. Further material details including transaction value, completion conditions, regulatory approvals required, and closure timeline are not yet publicly available in the primary source. Subsequent disclosures are expected per SEBI Listing Rules.

framework.note: central – Disclosure of material acquisitions within 30 minutes of approval by Board/Stock Exchange; subsidiary acquisitions must be disclosed if material to parent.
central – Board approval for acquisition of assets or investments beyond threshold limits; subsidiary acquisitions may require parent approval.
central – Directors' Report must disclose material acquisitions and related party transactions.
amended – Related party transaction framework; if seller is a related party of KPI Green, approval pathway and disclosures differ.

framework.ref: Foreign Direct Investment Policy (2020) / FEMA Act 1999
framework.note: If DEK has foreign ownership or acquirer has FDI routes, cross-border acquisition norms apply.
CCI review may be required if combined revenue/asset thresholds (₹2,000 cr revenue or ₹500 cr assets) are breached.

framework.ref: Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE) Regulations / Tariff Approval
framework.note: If DEK holds renewable energy contracts/tariffs, MNRE or state regulatory approval for change of control may be mandatory.
If DEK is under IBC proceedings, acquisition must be via NCLT-approved resolution plan.
